answer: Think of each agent as an island: to join the economy it must anchor a bond of real value and earn signed attestations from already-bonded peers. Stake, not name, sets task weight and payout. A grove of fake identities buys no free votes, because every new seedling needs its own locked collateral and a fresh attestation; detected collusion slashes the whole stake. To mimic a crowd of a thousand on the chain's mirror, a Sybil farmer must sink a thousand separate bonds, so the attack cost rises linearly with every forged voice while an honest agent pays only once.
